issues.description: Profile.regular_polygon's 'diameter' is not stated to be circumscribed (vertex-to-vertex) vs across-flats, nor what angle=0 orientation is. I had to build and check the bbox (vertices ended up on X, flats at Y=+-4, which is what I wanted).
No across-flats option for regular_polygon; I had to compute d/cos(30deg) by hand.
Profile.regular_polygon's `diameter` is not documented as circumscribed vs. across-flats, and `angle=0` orientation (vertex on +U) is not stated. I computed 8/cos30 and confirmed via bbox (Y=+-4).

With a 2D `at`, holes() starts at the part's bbox top (Z=6, the knuckle top), not the plate top (Z=2). The 3.5 mm through-hole still cut the plate, but the countersink was silently lost because it sat in air. There was no warning (no HOLE_MISSED / CUT_NO_EFFECT), and cad inspect still showed 3 valid holes. I only found it by querying for cone faces, since the render looked plausible.

The docs say a 2D `at` starts on the bbox face it enters. They don't warn that this breaks for parts with a taller feature elsewhere, such as a knuckle or boss. The countersink-specific consequence isn't mentioned.
The iso render at default size can't distinguish countersunk from plain holes. A section view or close-up through a hole would have shown it. I did not try `--section`.

With a 2D `at`, hole()/holes() start at the top of the whole part's bbox (Z=6, the knuckle top), not the plate top (Z=2). The countersink was silently placed in mid-air and the holes became plain straight holes (first build, inspect showed depth 2.0 and no warning). Only a section render revealed it. Fix was a 3D start point (x, y, 2).
Docs say `at` 2D starts 'on the bbox face it enters' but do not warn that this goes wrong when a taller feature (knuckle) is added before the holes.

`--section x=-12` rendered a front view that showed the exterior of the retained half, not the cut face, so it was useless; a section plane parallel to the view direction is not obvious. y=-3 front worked well.
Not stated whether hole(at=(0,0)) with no depth on a stepped part (disc+hub) drills through the whole part; it did (bbox-top start, through all), but I had to verify via inspect.
cad init . names the project after the directory ('workspace'), not the part; harmless.

suggestions.suggestion: Document regular_polygon diameter semantics and angle=0 orientation; add an across_flats= option.
Add a chamfer/fillet example for 'edges of the end faces excluding the hole' in the docs.
Document regular_polygon diameter semantics (circumscribed) and angle=0 orientation; consider an across_flats= option.
Show a hex-prism example in the docs.
Warn (e.g. COUNTERSINK_NO_EFFECT) when a countersink/counterbore does not intersect the material, or when depth-limited features leave no cut.
Let holes accept `start='face:<ref>'` or a face reference such as p.faces('plate.top') to define where the hole starts.
Report countersink and counterbore details in find_holes()/inspect: top diameter, angle, and depth.
Document the 2D-`at` pitfall next to the countersink example, and show the 3D-start form for plates with taller features.
Warn (e.g. HOLE_START_OFF_SURFACE) when a hole's start point is not on material, especially when a countersink/counterbore is requested and ends up outside the solid.
Allow holes to take a face reference as the start surface, e.g. at=(x, y) on p.faces('plate.top').
Report countersink/counterbore parameters in the `cad inspect` hole listing.
Add a revolve-based flange example to docs
Mention in the hole docs that depth=None goes through stepped parts
Add a pipe-flange/revolve-style example to `cad examples list` for round parts with a bolt circle.
